note: Per-architecture SM DRAM rate facts, regenerated by `tools/bench/warp_inflight/warp_inflight.py regenerate` from the committed probe runs in src/core/data/warp_inflight/ (warp_inflight_<arch>.txt: the architecture's reference card; warp_inflight_<arch>_<card>.txt: another card of it, a transfer check; all written by `warp_inflight.py run`, never edited by hand), read by core/sm_rate_facts.h for the decode price's per-SM bound min(P, W x b_w / (L0 + (b_w - 512 B) / F)) with b_w at most b_w_max where a warp saturates (kernel_roofline.h dram_time, #690, #771). sm_dram_bytes_per_clock_free / _placed: P, the largest rate one SM reached at k = 1 (any variant, any W) over the SM clock of that row, with the L1-largest carve-out (`free`) and the shared-largest one (`placed`); sm_dram_gbps_* and sm_mhz_* are the rate and clock it was read from. dram_stream_latency_ns: L0, the run's own fetch time of one warp alone on one SM with one 16-byte streaming load a lane in flight (free, k = 1, chain1, W = 1): the loads the law prices, not the ISA table's pointer chase (dram_tlbwarm_latency_ns_w1, 8-24 % shorter on the same card). max_warp_bytes_in_flight: b_w_max, the most bytes in flight one warp alone reached (b_w at W = 1 by Little's law on L0, the largest over every variant and both carve-outs). warp_fill_bytes_per_clock: F, the rate a lone warp's window fills at past its first warp-wide load (fill_rate: the least-squares ns a further byte costs over the run's chains at k = 1, W = 1, at chain1's SM clock; 17-19 B a clock on every architecture, about 0.55 P; the 8- and 4-byte chains of probe 7 show it goes with the bytes, not the loads). warp_bytes_saturated: the warp saturates, so b_w_max caps the bytes the law counts. In a row whose run has chain8 and chain16 (probe 5 on), cap_test sets each chain's lone-warp b_w against the two-latency bound count x L0 / (2 x the ISA table's dram_tlbwarm_latency_ns_w1): a warp held to fewer loads than the chain's count reads at or under it (cap_test: each chain's reading, its bound and the latency's source). The bound proves that direction only, so a reading under it alone is no cap: the verdict is a cap only where both chains read at or under their bounds and the ring rule agrees, no cap where both read above, and undecided otherwise (the ring rule then decides); this tightens the rule frozen in 665e190b after the codex review of #765, and changes no committed verdict. The test decides only with the card's own ISA latency; with another card's (a transfer) it is reported, and the ring rule decides. In an earlier run's row, it saturates where the 4-load ring keeps less than x1.5 of the 2-load ring's b_w at W = 1 (ring4_over_ring2_w1; the midpoint between no gain and the doubling its count gives: sm_70 x1.20, sm_120a x1.00 saturate, sm_75 / sm_86 / sm_89 x1.80-1.81 do not); elsewhere b_w_max is a lower bound of the warp's limit and caps nothing. ring2_* / chain4_* / ring4_*: b_w at W = 1 of the two-slot ring with two loads a lane a slot (2048 B a warp by count), of four loads a lane in one chain (2048 B) and of the 4-load ring (4096 B), and the largest W up to which every ring2 row keeps 0.9 of it. ring2_rows, ring4_rows: those rows at k = 1, [W, GB/s an SM, SM MHz], the measurement the law's check reads (tests/ops/linear/test_kernel_roofline.cpp check 8). transfer: the other cards' runs of the architecture, their ring rows, the law of this row against them (law over measured: the lowest, the highest at W = 1, the highest), and `refuted` when any of their rows falls outside the check's bounds (the law below the row by more than 5 %, above it by more than x1.05 at W = 1 or x1.25 anywhere): a refuted row is no fact of the architecture, and its boards keep the legacy DRAM law. Provenance Measured for every run, with its source file, card, probe version, nvcc, driver, runtime and the sha256 of the warp_inflight.cu it was built from; a board of the architecture other than the reference card is priced by the reference row, a transfer. tests/test_warp_inflight.py pins that the table equals its regeneration and that every committed run is of the checked-in probe or of an earlier one it records (warp_inflight.py EARLIER_PROBES: that version's source sha256 and variants).
